memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, 'This is how your slave treated me,' he burned with anger. Joseph's master took him and put him in prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined. But while Joseph was there in the prison," - Gen 39:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Potiphar believes his wife's lie, burns with anger, and throws Joseph into prison. And here we must sit for a moment with the sheer injustice of it. Joseph did everything right. He resisted temptation, honoured his master, refused to sin against God — and his reward is a prison cell. The innocent man is punished; the guilty woman goes free. This is one of the hardest truths in the whole story: sometimes we do the right thing and suffer for it anyway.

If you have ever obeyed God and then faced loss, misunderstanding, or punishment for it, you know how bewildering this can feel. We half expect that doing right will lead to good outcomes. But Joseph reminds us that faithfulness is not always rewarded in this life the way we would like. "It is better, if it is God's will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil" (1 Pet 3:17).

Yet notice how the verse ends — not with a full stop, but with a hopeful turn: "But while Joseph was there in the prison..." That little word "but" is the hinge of hope. Joseph's story was not over in that cell. God was still with him, still at work, even in this unjust place.

When you suffer for doing right, hold on to the "but" of God. The prison is not the end of your story. The same God who was with Joseph goes with you into every unjust place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever done right and suffered for it anyway?
2. Can I trust God even when faithfulness is not rewarded as I hoped?
3. Where do I need to hold on to the "but" of God in my situation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when I do right and suffer for it, help me not to lose heart. Thank You that my hardest chapter is never the end. Be with me in every unjust place, and let me hold on to Your "but." Amen.
